title: The perceptron, 1958: promise before hardware
summary: In 1958 the press suggested a Navy-funded perceptron might one day walk and talk. A 1969 book showed single-layer perceptrons cannot learn XOR.

beats.say: In nineteen fifty eight, a newspaper suggested a machine might walk.
Frank Rosenblatt built the perceptron at the Cornell Aeronautical Laboratory.
The U.S. Office of Naval Research funded the project.
beats.cap: Funded by the Office of Naval Research

beats.say: The Mark one machine had four hundred photocells in a twenty by twenty grid.
Its first public demonstration, in July nineteen fifty eight, ran on an I.B.M. seven oh four.
It learned to tell whether a dot was on the left or right.
beats.cap: Task: dot on the left or right

beats.say: The New York Times suggested the Navy expected it to walk, talk and see.
In nineteen sixty nine, a book showed single layer perceptrons cannot learn X.O.R.
The book contributed to a sharp drop in neural network funding.
Big promises first. A hard limit came later.

claims.note: Wikipedia, Perceptron: Mark I had 400 photocells in a 20x20 grid
Guinness: first public demonstration on 7 July 1958 on a 5-ton IBM 704 that simulated the hardware

facts.claim: Frank Rosenblatt developed the perceptron at the Cornell Aeronautical Laboratory, funded by the US Office of Naval Research
facts.note: Wikipedia, Perceptron: Rosenblatt, Cornell Aeronautical Laboratory; Office of Naval Research funded the project

facts.claim: The Mark I Perceptron had 400 photocells in a 20x20 grid
facts.note: Wikipedia, Perceptron: 400 photocells in a 20x20 grid as sensory units

facts.claim: The first public demonstration was on 7 July 1958 on an IBM 704 that simulated the hardware, and the task was telling whether a dot was on the left or right of a card
facts.note: Guinness World Records: first demonstrated 7 July 1958; IBM 704; read 20x20 photocell scans of cards with a dot and told left from right

facts.claim: The New York Times suggested the Navy expected the perceptron could eventually walk, talk, see and reproduce itself
facts.note: Wikipedia, Perceptron: 1958 NYT report based on Rosenblatt's statements at a Navy press conference

facts.claim: The 1969 book Perceptrons by Minsky and Papert showed single-layer perceptrons cannot learn XOR and contributed to a sharp decline in neural network funding
facts.note: Wikipedia, Perceptron: 1969 book; single-layer limitation (XOR); contributed to decline in funding and interest until the 1980s
